title: Litotes and Hedged Assertion: nem éppen, alighanem, mondhatni

sections.title: The Power of Litotes (nem éppen)
sections.content: Litotes (understatement through negation) is a hallmark of sophisticated Hungarian commentary. Instead of blunt criticism ('Ez nagyon rossz volt'), an educated speaker says 'Nem éppen volt zseniális' (It was not exactly brilliant). Saying 'nem éppen olcsó' signals that something is prohibitively expensive. The pitch falls on 'nem' and rises ironically on the adjective.

sections.title: Hedged Probability: 'alighanem' and 'mondhatni'
sections.content: 'Alighanem' expresses strong probability tempered with modesty ('in all likelihood / most probably'): 'Alighanem igaza van' (In all likelihood he is right). 'Mondhatni' functions as a parenthetical hedge ('so to speak / one might say'): 'Ez a döntés, mondhatni, elhamarkodott volt.' Together, they allow a writer to critique without appearing overly aggressive.

sections.title: Litotes and Understatement Patterns
rows: not exactly / far from (polite or ironic negation)
in all likelihood / most probably (hedged assertion)
so to speak / one might say (stylistic moderation)

items.spanish: A szálloda szolgáltatásai nem éppen a luxust idézték.
items.english: The hotel's services did not exactly evoke luxury.

items.spanish: Alighanem elfelejtette, hogy a határidő tegnap lejárt.
items.english: In all likelihood, he forgot that the deadline expired yesterday.

items.spanish: A helyzet, mondhatni, meglehetősen bonyolulttá vált.
items.english: The situation has become, so to speak, rather complicated.

items.spanish: Az író fanyar humorral mutatta be a nemesség gyengeségeit.
items.english: The writer depicted the nobility's weaknesses with wry humor.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Pay attention to context: 'nem éppen zseniális' is rarely neutral; in Hungarian culture, it is an unmistakable signal of ironic disapproval.
